description.value:
A circlet of bent wire, ribbon and things that were probably never jewellery, which somehow looks deliberate on her and ridiculous on everyone else. It is warm when she is delighted and warmer when she is about to do something unwise.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Alice)

It is not a crown because somebody crowned her. It is a crown because she decided it was one, and the world has so far declined to argue.

Marginal note, Wayreth Deep Catalogue

How this item works

This is a legacy item. It keeps everything from earlier states unless a later feature says it replaces one, and its charge pool and each feature unlock on their own as Alice gains levels — Foundry hides an activity until its level band is reached, so the sheet only ever shows what is currently available.

Legacy Save DC: 8 + proficiency bonus + her spellcasting ability modifier.

Dormant — Uncommon, levels 3–5

Wonder Charges: 3, all of them returning at dawn.

Borrowed Cantrips

Alice learns druidcraft and minor illusion. They count as sorcerer spells for her and do not count against her cantrips known. If she already knows either, she may replace that cantrip with another non-damaging bard, druid or sorcerer cantrip.

Pocketful of Nonsense

As a bonus action, expend 1 Wonder Charge to produce one effect:

  • Hop. Alice or a willing creature within 30 feet moves up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space Alice can see. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks but cannot pass through solid objects.
  • Fetch. One unattended object Alice can see within 30 feet weighing no more than 10 pounds flies into her hand. An object being worn, carried, secured or magically anchored cannot be affected.
  • Distract. One creature Alice can see within 30 feet has disadvantage on its next opportunity attack or Wisdom (Perception) check before the start of Alice's next turn.

Oops

When Alice or a creature she can see within 30 feet makes an ability check, Alice can use her reaction and expend 1 charge to add 1d4 after seeing the roll but before the outcome is declared.

Little Places

Alice can move through the space of any creature larger than herself, and squeezing costs her no additional movement.

Awakened — Rare, levels 6–9

Awakening: Alice openly acknowledges something genuinely important to her rather than hiding it behind humour, bravado or performance, and then acts upon it.

Wonder Charges: 5, all of them returning at dawn.

Rabbit Hole

When Alice takes damage, she can use her reaction and expend 2 charges to teleport up to 30 feet to an unoccupied space she can see. If this takes her outside the triggering effect's range, it does not prevent the triggering damage. After teleporting, Alice can become invisible until the beginning of her next turn or until she attacks, deals damage or casts a spell.

Improvised Solution

When Alice attempts an unconventional but physically or magically plausible use of an object, spell or environmental feature, she can expend 1 charge to gain advantage on one associated ability check or spellcasting ability check. If the improvised action instead immediately forces exactly one creature to make a saving throw, Alice can impose disadvantage on that save. Once this feature succeeds, it cannot be used again until she finishes a short or long rest.

That's Mine Now

Alice can expend 1 charge to cast mage hand, except that the hand can carry 30 pounds, its range is 60 feet, and Alice can make it appear as any Tiny hand, paw, claw or similarly shaped appendage. It lasts 10 minutes and requires no concentration.

Exalted — Very Rare, levels 10–14

Awakening: Alice deliberately risks something she values because another person's happiness, safety or sense of wonder matters more to her than avoiding hurt herself.

Wonder Charges: 7, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn rather than all expended charges.

Make-Believe

As an action, Alice expends 3 charges and describes a mundane object she can see or has personally encountered before. The created object appears in an unoccupied space within 30 feet and lasts 10 minutes, functioning as a normal nonmagical object of its type. It:

  • must fit within a 10-foot cube;
  • can weigh no more than 500 pounds;
  • cannot have a market value above 100 gp;
  • cannot contain poison, explosives, alchemical substances or other consumable compounds;
  • cannot be a spell component with a listed monetary value;
  • cannot be a firearm or siege weapon;
  • cannot duplicate a magic item;
  • cannot be a functioning complex mechanism requiring more than five independently moving components.

A created object cannot be sold and vanishes if broken into separate components. A ladder, rowboat, door, table, bridge section, mattress, cage, giant umbrella, wheelbarrow or ridiculous throne are all fair game.

It Was Worth a Try

Once per short or long rest, when Alice fails an ability check by 5 or less, she can decide that the attempt succeeds instead — in the messiest reasonable way. The DM may introduce a complication, but the complication cannot negate the success. This is not usable on attack rolls or saving throws.

Follow the Kender

When Alice uses Rabbit Hole, she may expend 1 additional charge to take one willing creature within 5 feet with her. Both creatures arrive in unoccupied spaces within 5 feet of one another.

Legendary — Legendary, level 15+

Awakening: Alice willingly chooses genuine belonging despite knowing that loving people gives the world something it can take from her.

Wonder Charges: 9, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn.

The World Is More Interesting This Way

Make-Believe improves: the maximum dimensions become a 20-foot cube, the maximum weight becomes 2,000 pounds, the maximum mundane value becomes 500 gp, and the duration becomes 1 hour. Alice can also create a simple structure composed of connected mundane parts, such as a small cottage, bridge, stage, wagon or sailing boat. It still cannot create valuable materials, creatures, food with magical effects, siege weapons, spell components, magic items or advanced machinery.

You Can't Take This From Me

When Alice or a creature she can see within 30 feet fails a saving throw against being charmed, frightened, possessed or magically controlled, Alice can use her reaction and expend 3 charges. The creature rerolls the saving throw with advantage. On a success, it also gains immunity to that specific creature's charm, fear, possession and control effects until the next dawn.

Happily Ever After

Once per long rest, when Alice or an ally within 30 feet would be reduced to 0 hit points, Alice can declare "That's not how this story ends." The creature instead drops to 1 hit point, immediately gains temporary hit points equal to twice Alice's sorcerer level, and may use its reaction to move up to its speed without provoking opportunity attacks. This is not resurrection. Alice cannot stop death forever. She can occasionally insist that this is not the page where it happens.

Vault Record

Classification: Legacy item, bound to Alice. Rules: D&D 5e (2014). Origin: A gift kept long past the point where keeping it made sense.

description.value:
A brass compass with a needle that has never once pointed north. Ispin Greenshield carried it, and the only instruction that came with it was that it should be given to somebody who would worry about the answer.

Wondrous item and arcane focus, legacy item (requires attunement by Solanthis)

It does not tell you where you are going. It tells you who is about to need you.

Ispin Greenshield, to a young man who asked the wrong question

How this item works

This is a legacy item. It keeps everything from earlier states unless a later feature says it replaces one, and its charge pool and each feature unlock on their own as Solanthis gains levels — Foundry hides an activity until its level band is reached, so the sheet only ever shows what is currently available.

Legacy Save DC: 8 + proficiency bonus + his spellcasting ability modifier.

Dormant — Uncommon, levels 3–5

Promise Charges: 3, all of them returning at dawn.

The Compass

The brass compass serves as an arcane focus. Its needle points toward whichever creature within 60 feet Solanthis sincerely believes is in the greatest immediate physical danger. This gives no supernatural knowledge of hidden creatures.

Forewarned

Solanthis gains a +1 bonus to initiative and cannot be surprised while conscious.

Not Them

When a creature Solanthis can see within 30 feet is hit by an attack, he can use his reaction and expend 1 charge to grant it +2 AC against the triggering attack, potentially turning the hit into a miss.

Prepared Mind

At the end of each long rest, choose acid, cold, fire, lightning, necrotic, psychic, radiant or thunder. Once before Solanthis' next long rest, when he or a creature within 30 feet takes the selected damage type, he can use his reaction to grant that creature resistance to the triggering damage.

Awakened — Rare, levels 6–9

Awakening: Solanthis possesses the means to force someone to follow what he believes is the correct course, and deliberately allows that person to make the decision themselves.

Promise Charges: 5, all of them returning at dawn.

I Planned for This

When a creature Solanthis can see within 30 feet fails a saving throw, he can use his reaction and expend 2 charges to allow it to reroll. The new roll must be used.

Contingency Pocket

Once per long rest, Solanthis may produce a mundane object he could reasonably have acquired. It must cost no more than 25 gp, weigh no more than 10 pounds, fit inside a backpack, and not be a weapon, armour, poison or spell component with a listed cost. It disappears at the next dawn if not consumed or destroyed. Narratively, he prepared it earlier.

Calculated Intervention

Not Them improves: when it turns the attack into a miss, the protected creature may immediately move 5 feet without provoking opportunity attacks. This replaces the Dormant version of Not Them.

Exalted — Very Rare, levels 10–14

Awakening: Solanthis accepts a serious personal risk because his preparation can protect others, despite having a safer option available to him.

Promise Charges: 7, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn.

Contingency

After a long rest, Solanthis may designate two willing creatures, including himself, that he can see. For each, choose one contingency:

  • Escape. When reduced below half hit points, the creature may immediately move up to half its speed without provoking opportunity attacks.
  • Brace. When it fails a Strength, Dexterity or Constitution saving throw, it adds 1d6, potentially succeeding.
  • Mind. When it fails an Intelligence, Wisdom or Charisma saving throw, it adds 1d6, potentially succeeding.
  • Endure. When reduced to 0 hit points without being killed outright, it drops to 1 hit point instead.

Each contingency triggers once and then disappears. A creature can have only one at a time.

No One Gets Left Behind

As an action, Solanthis can expend 3 charges. For 1 minute a 20-foot-radius protective field moves with him, and while inside it his allies ignore nonmagical difficult terrain, have advantage on death saving throws, cannot have their speed reduced below 10 feet unless incapacitated, and gain +1 AC. He must concentrate on this as though concentrating on a spell.

There Was Another Way

When Solanthis casts a spell that deals damage, he may choose any number of creatures he can see to automatically succeed on their saving throws against that spell and take no damage if they would normally take half. Once used, this cannot be used again until a short or long rest.

Legendary — Legendary, level 15+

Awakening: Solanthis faces a situation in which imposing his will would genuinely be easier and possibly safer, but finds a way to protect people without taking their agency from them.

Promise Charges: 9, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn.

Grand Contingency

Solanthis can maintain contingencies on a number of creatures equal to his proficiency bonus rather than two. This replaces Contingency.

I Accounted for That

Once per long rest, after a creature Solanthis can see within 60 feet rolls a natural 1, suffers a critical hit, fails a saving throw or is reduced to 0 hit points, he can use his reaction and declare that he prepared for precisely this possibility. Choose one:

  • the natural 1 becomes a 10;
  • the critical hit becomes a normal hit;
  • the failed save is rerolled with advantage;
  • the creature drops to 1 hit point.

The Promise

Once per long rest, as an action, Solanthis chooses up to six willing creatures within 30 feet. For 1 minute each gains resistance to one damage type chosen individually when this begins, +2 AC, advantage on death saving throws, and immunity to being frightened. Solanthis gains none of these benefits. The effect requires concentration. At his absolute strongest, his greatest magic is still about everyone else getting home.

Vault Record

Classification: Legacy item, bound to Solanthis. Rules: D&D 5e (2014). Origin: Ispin Greenshield's own, handed on rather than inherited.

description.value:
A steel coin with no face and no crown, worn smooth on both sides. Flipped, it lands on its edge often enough that Jinx has stopped finding it funny and started finding it useful.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Jinx)

Every coin has two answers. This one has been holding a third in reserve.

How this item works

This is a legacy item. It keeps everything from earlier states unless a later feature says it replaces one, and its charge pool and each feature unlock on their own as Jinx gains levels — Foundry hides an activity until its level band is reached, so the sheet only ever shows what is currently available.

Legacy Save DC: 8 + proficiency bonus + his spellcasting ability modifier.

Dormant — Uncommon, levels 3–5

Luck Charges: 3, all of them returning at dawn.

Double or Nothing

After Jinx fails an attack roll, ability check or saving throw, he may expend 1 charge and roll 1d6. On a 1–2 the original roll stands. On a 3–6 he rerolls the d20 and adds 1d4. He must use the new result.

Liar's Coin

Jinx learns minor illusion. Once per short or long rest, when making a Deception, Performance or Sleight of Hand check, he may treat a d20 result of 9 or lower as 10.

Surely Magic Is Relevant

Jinx can expend 1 charge before making an ability check to use Intelligence in place of its normal ability. He must provide some remotely plausible magical explanation.

Awakened — Rare, levels 6–9

Awakening: Jinx has a genuine opportunity to escape serious danger and deliberately stays because something or someone matters more.

Luck Charges: 5, all of them returning at dawn.

Push Your Luck

After Double or Nothing turns a failure into a success, Jinx may Push. Roll 1d6:

  • 1–3: the success remains, but Jinx takes 2d6 psychic damage;
  • 4–5: the success remains and the Luck Charge is refunded;
  • 6: the success becomes extraordinary — an attack becomes a critical hit, and an ability check or saving throw is treated as though the d20 rolled 20.

The psychic damage ignores resistance.

That's Not How That Spell Works

Once per long rest when casting a spell, Jinx may choose one:

  • change acid, cold, fire, lightning or thunder damage into another type on that list;
  • double the spell's range, to a maximum of 300 feet;
  • remove its verbal component;
  • remove its somatic component.

Exalted — Very Rare, levels 10–14

Awakening: Jinx knowingly takes a dangerous magical risk for something more important than proving that he can.

Luck Charges: 7, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn.

That's DEFINITELY Not How That Spell Works

That's Not How That Spell Works can now be used a number of times per long rest equal to Jinx's proficiency bonus, but only once per spell. It also gains:

  • Bend. If a spell affects a line, cone, cube or sphere, Jinx can exclude a number of creatures equal to his Intelligence modifier, minimum one.
  • Stretch. A spell with a duration of 1 minute or longer and no concentration requirement has its duration doubled, to a maximum of 24 hours.

This replaces the Awakened version.

All In

When Jinx uses Double or Nothing, he may spend 2 charges instead of 1. He immediately rerolls the d20 with advantage and adds 1d4. If both advantage dice would fail the original DC or AC, Jinx suffers 3d6 psychic damage and cannot use Double or Nothing again until the end of his next turn.

I Meant To Do That

Once per short or long rest, after Jinx triggers a trap, activates an unknown magical effect or causes an unintended magical consequence, he may gain resistance to all damage caused by that initial triggering effect and advantage on its first saving throw. The accident still happens. Jinx is simply astonishingly good at surviving Jinx.

Legendary — Legendary, level 15+

Awakening: Jinx reaches a moment where chance, magic and bravado could give him extraordinary personal power, and deliberately gambles it for somebody else.

Luck Charges: 9, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn.

The Impossible Bet

Once per long rest, before rolling a d20, Jinx can announce an Impossible Bet, naming the specific action and intended outcome. Roll two d20s. Jinx chooses one; the other becomes a Debt Die. Before Jinx's next long rest the DM may replace one d20 Jinx rolls with the Debt Die, after Jinx rolls but before the outcome is determined. If the unused Debt Die was a natural 20, the DM cannot use it and the debt disappears. Jinx literally borrows luck from his future.

Rewrite the Rules

Once per long rest, when Jinx casts a spell of 5th level or lower, he can apply two different That's Not How That Spell Works modifications to it.

The Coin Lands Sideways

Once per long rest, when Jinx rolls a natural 1 or a natural 20, he can flip the result: 1 becomes 20, or 20 becomes 1. Why would he voluntarily turn a 20 into a 1? Because there will eventually be a reason.

Vault Record

Classification: Legacy item, bound to Jinx. Rules: D&D 5e (2014). Origin: Won, allegedly fairly, from somebody who was very keen to be rid of it.

description.value:
An iron lantern whose flame gives almost no heat and throws the wrong shadows. It brightens near the recently dead, which is a property nobody asked it to have.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Sylas)

Everyone else sees a cursed altar and says don't. He sees an experiment that hasn't been run yet. The Lantern was made for the second kind of person.

How this item works

This is a legacy item. It keeps everything from earlier states unless a later feature says it replaces one, and its charge pool and each feature unlock on their own as Sylas gains levels — Foundry hides an activity until its level band is reached, so the sheet only ever shows what is currently available.

Legacy Save DC: 8 + proficiency bonus + his spellcasting ability modifier.

Dormant — Uncommon, levels 3–5

Vigil Charges: 3, all of them restored at dusk.

Mortuary Light

By touching a corpse for 1 minute, Sylas learns its approximate time of death, whether death primarily resulted from violence, disease, poison, magic or natural causes, and whether necromancy affected it after death.

Shepherd's Questions

Sylas can expend 1 charge to gain advantage on one Arcana, Investigation, Medicine, Nature or Religion check concerning a corpse, an undead creature, a curse, a planar phenomenon, a supernatural disease or a ritual.

Knowledge Has a Price

After failing such a check, Sylas can take 1d6 necrotic damage per proficiency bonus to reroll it. This damage cannot be reduced or prevented. Once used, this feature cannot be used again until he finishes a short or long rest.

Awakened — Rare, levels 6–9

Awakening: Sylas knowingly accepts a meaningful personal consequence in exchange for knowledge capable of protecting another person.

Vigil Charges: 5, all of them restored at dusk.

Ask the Dead

Sylas can expend 3 charges to cast speak with dead.

Hold the Door

When a creature within 30 feet would drop to 0 hit points, Sylas can use his reaction and expend 2 charges. It instead drops to 1. Sylas takes 2d8 necrotic damage that cannot be reduced or prevented.

Forbidden Inquiry

Once per long rest, Sylas can spend one Hit Die while examining a creature, corpse, object or supernatural phenomenon for 1 minute. He may ask the DM one factual question concerning its nature, origin, condition, vulnerabilities or magical properties. The answer must be truthful but need not reveal information that no available divinatory magic could reasonably determine. The Hit Die remains spent normally.

Exalted — Very Rare, levels 10–14

Awakening: Sylas encounters something that fundamentally challenges his understanding of death or cosmic order and chooses understanding over denial without surrendering his principles.

Vigil Charges: 7, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dusk.

Take Their Burden

As an action, Sylas can touch a willing creature and expend 3 charges to transfer one of the following from it to himself: blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, poisoned, one disease, or one curse affecting only that creature. The original target is freed. Sylas receives the condition, disease or curse for its remaining duration and receives no saving throw against the initial transfer. If the effect requires ongoing saves, Sylas makes them normally.

The Soul Waits

When a creature dies within 30 feet, Sylas can use his reaction and expend 3 charges. For 1 minute its soul cannot be unwillingly transformed, trapped or consumed, its corpse cannot become undead, and resurrection magic cast upon it requires no material component worth 300 gp or less. This does not resurrect the creature.

Autopsy of the Impossible

After observing a creature for 1 minute, Sylas may expend 2 charges to learn two of the following:

  • damage immunities;
  • damage resistances;
  • damage vulnerabilities;
  • condition immunities;
  • highest saving throw;
  • lowest saving throw;
  • whether it has Legendary Resistance;
  • creature type;
  • one special trait chosen by the DM that materially defines the creature.

A creature cannot be examined this way again until Sylas finishes a long rest.

Legendary — Legendary, level 15+

Awakening: Sylas is given the opportunity to violate the natural boundary of death for something he desperately wants, and consciously defines where his line lies.

Vigil Charges: 9, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dusk.

Shepherd Between Worlds

Sylas constantly sees 30 feet into the Ethereal Plane, and can perceive invisible undead within 30 feet even if he cannot otherwise see invisible creatures.

Not Yet

When a creature within 60 feet dies, Sylas can use his reaction and expend 5 charges. Its body falls dead normally, but its soul remains beside him as a visible spectral presence until the end of his next turn. Before then, Sylas may use an action to return the soul. The creature returns to life with 1 hit point, 2 levels of exhaustion, and no benefit from healing until the end of its next turn. Once Sylas successfully restores a creature this way, he cannot use Not Yet again until 7 days have passed. This cannot restore a creature that died of old age or whose soul is unwilling or unavailable.

Let Me Understand

Once per long rest, Sylas can spend 3 Hit Dice and spend 1 minute studying a creature, artifact, corpse, curse or supernatural phenomenon. The DM must reveal three materially useful truths concerning it. At least one must concern a weakness, limitation, cost, method of destruction, method of cure or means by which it can be opposed, if such information exists. Sylas' ultimate weapon is not death. It is knowing what everyone else was afraid to examine.

effects.description: Climbing speed equal to Clipper's walking speed. Shipped disabled because a movement effect cannot gate itself on level the way the charge pool does; enable it when the Knot awakens.

description.value:
A short length of road-rope tied in a knot nobody has managed to copy. It never frays, and it pulls very slightly towards wherever he slept last.

Wondrous item, legacy item (requires attunement by Clipper)

Roads are not for leaving. They are the part of leaving that lets you come back.

How this item works

This is a legacy item. It keeps everything from earlier states unless a later feature says it replaces one, and its charge pool and each feature unlock on their own as Clipper gains levels — Foundry hides an activity until its level band is reached, so the sheet only ever shows what is currently available.

Legacy Save DC: 8 + proficiency bonus + his Wisdom modifier.

Dormant — Uncommon, levels 3–5

Trail Charges: 3, all of them restored at dawn.

Never Lost

Clipper always knows north, and the direction and approximate distance to the place where he most recently completed a long rest, provided it is on the same plane. He has advantage on Survival checks to navigate and to follow tracks.

Rope Remembers

Clipper can touch the Knot to a location for 1 minute. For 24 hours he knows its direction and approximate distance while on the same plane. Only one location can be remembered at a time.

Get Them Through

As a bonus action, Clipper can expend 1 charge and choose himself or one creature within 30 feet. Until the end of its next turn, difficult terrain costs it no additional movement, standing costs only 5 feet, and it does not provoke opportunity attacks from one creature Clipper chooses.

Awakened — Rare, levels 6–9

Awakening: Clipper willingly gives up progress toward an important objective to return for someone or something that would otherwise be left behind.

Trail Charges: 5, all of them restored at dawn.

Follow Me

When Clipper takes the Dash action, he can expend 1 charge. Up to a number of willing creatures equal to his proficiency bonus, within 30 feet, can use their reactions to move up to half their speeds toward Clipper without provoking opportunity attacks.

Find the Missing

Clipper can hold an object belonging to a creature, concentrate for 1 minute and expend 2 charges. For 1 hour he knows the general direction of that creature while it is within 5 miles on the same plane. If it is dead, he senses its remains instead. This does not reveal distance or obstacles.

Sure Footing

Clipper gains a climbing speed equal to his walking speed. This one passive is shipped as a switched-off effect on the item — enable Sure Footing in the item's Effects tab when the Knot awakens.

Exalted — Very Rare, levels 10–14

Awakening: Clipper successfully guides others through a journey from which he personally has compelling reason not to return.

Trail Charges: 7, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn.

Waymarks

Clipper can establish a number of permanent Waymarks equal to his proficiency bonus. Establishing one requires 10 minutes at the location. He always knows the direction and approximate distance to every Waymark while on the same plane. Creating one beyond his maximum erases one of his choice.

Walk My Road

As an action, Clipper can expend 3 charges and choose up to his proficiency bonus in willing creatures within 30 feet. For 1 hour their walking speeds increase by 10 feet, nonmagical difficult terrain costs them no extra movement, they have advantage on checks and saves against environmental hazards caused by travel, and they cannot become lost except through powerful magical interference.

I'm Coming Back

When a creature affected by Find the Missing is reduced to 0 hit points, Clipper immediately knows. For the remaining duration his speed increases by 10 feet whenever he moves directly toward that creature, and opportunity attacks against him have disadvantage.

Legendary — Legendary, level 15+

Awakening: Clipper must choose between completing an extraordinary journey and returning for someone who needs him — and chooses to return, knowing the opportunity may never come again.

Trail Charges: 9, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn.

There Is Always a Road

Once per long rest, Clipper can spend 1 minute holding the Knot and expend 5 charges. Choose one of his Waymarks on the same plane within 100 miles. A shimmering trail appears; Clipper and up to eight willing creatures who follow it travel through an impossible shortcut and emerge at the Waymark after 10 minutes. This is not teleportation for mechanical purposes — the travellers physically traverse a supernatural road, and cannot interact with the outside world during the journey.

Nobody Gets Lost

All willing creatures within 30 feet of Clipper cannot become magically lost, know the direction to Clipper, and have advantage on saving throws against magical effects that would teleport or banish them against their will.

Bring Them Home

Once per long rest, Clipper can designate up to six willing creatures he can see. For 8 hours he always knows their direction and approximate distance while they remain on the same plane. If one becomes unconscious, dies, changes planes or is forcibly teleported, Clipper knows immediately.

effects.name: Carry the Impossible
effects.description: Two sizes larger for carrying, pushing, dragging and lifting from level 6 (x4), and Gargantuan from level 15 (x8). The multiplier is a dnd5e formula field, so this gates itself on Kattal's level and needs no switching on.

description.value:
A black iron spike the length of a forearm, with a flattened head that has been struck a great many times. It is the second thing of Ispin Greenshield's to leave his hands, and the only one he never explained.

Rod, legacy item (requires attunement by Kattal)

A nail's whole purpose is to stay where it was put. Everything else about it is decoration.

Ispin Greenshield

How this item works

This is a legacy item. It keeps everything from earlier states unless a later feature says it replaces one, and its charge pool and each feature unlock on their own as Kattal gains levels — Foundry hides an activity until its level band is reached, so the sheet only ever shows what is currently available.

Legacy Save DC: 8 + proficiency bonus + his Strength modifier.

Dormant — Uncommon, levels 3–5

Bastion Charges: 3, all of them restored at dawn.

Immovable Rod

The Nail retains the normal properties of an immovable rod. You can use an action to press the button, fixing the Nail in place until you or another creature uses an action to press the button again. It can hold up to 8,000 pounds; more weight causes it to deactivate and fall. A creature can use an action to make a DC 30 Strength check, moving the fixed Nail up to 10 feet on a success.

Brace

While Kattal is holding the activated Rod, he has advantage on checks and saves against being knocked prone, reduces forced movement against himself by 10 feet, and has advantage on Strength checks made to lift, hold, push or prevent something from moving.

Catch Them

When a creature within Kattal's reach falls, is knocked prone or is forcibly moved, he can use his reaction and expend 1 charge. A willing creature is automatically caught. An unwilling creature makes a Strength or Dexterity saving throw against Kattal's Legacy Save DC; on a failure he catches it. A falling creature stops falling if Kattal is capable of supporting its weight.

Awakened — Rare, levels 6–9

Awakening: Kattal holds something dangerous back, or supports something failing, when releasing it would be safer for him.

Bastion Charges: 5, all of them restored at dawn.

Behind Me

As a bonus action, Kattal expends 1 charge and designates a creature within 5 feet. Until the beginning of his next turn, that creature gains half cover while it remains within 5 feet of him.

No.

When Kattal fails a Strength check or Strength saving throw, he can expend 2 charges to treat the d20 as a 15.

Carry the Impossible

Kattal counts as two sizes larger when determining carrying capacity and how much weight he can push, drag or lift.

Exalted — Very Rare, levels 10–14

Awakening: Kattal deliberately makes himself the barrier between overwhelming danger and creatures unable to withstand it.

Bastion Charges: 7, regaining 1d6 + 1 at dawn.

You Go Through Me

As a bonus action, Kattal can expend 3 charges to enter Bastion Stance for 1 minute. While in this stance:

  • Kattal cannot be forcibly moved or knocked prone while conscious unless he chooses;
  • allies within 5 feet gain half cover;
  • hostile creatures treat the area within 10 feet of Kattal as difficult terrain;
  • when a creature within Kattal's reach attacks an ally, Kattal can use his reaction to make one melee weapon attack against that creature.

The stance ends early if Kattal becomes incapacitated.

Hold It!

When a Huge or smaller creature attempts to move through Kattal's reach, he can use his reaction to make an Athletics check contested by its Athletics or Acrobatics. On a success its speed becomes 0 for the remainder of the turn. He may attempt this against a Gargantuan creature by expending 1 Bastion Charge.

Living Rampart

When Kattal would provide half cover to an ally, he may choose to provide three-quarters cover instead. Until the beginning of his next turn, attacks that miss that ally specifically because of this cover bonus hit Kattal instead if the attack roll would hit his AC.

Legendary — Legendary, level 15+

Awakening: Kattal stands against something he cannot reasonably overpower because someone behind him needs him to remain standing.

Bastion Charges: 9, regaining 1d8 + 1 at dawn.

The Unmoving

While conscious and touching the ground, Kattal cannot be forcibly moved or knocked prone unless he chooses, has advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws, and counts as Gargantuan solely for carrying, pushing, dragging, lifting and determining what creatures he can grapple or physically impede. He does not gain Gargantuan reach, weapon damage or occupied space.

I Said No

Once per short or long rest, when Kattal fails a Strength saving throw or Strength check, he can choose to succeed instead. If the effect would move, crush, drag or physically overwhelm him, he may additionally prevent that effect from moving through his space until the beginning of his next turn.

The Last Wall

Once per long rest, as a bonus action, Kattal activates the Nail for 1 minute. He gains resistance to all damage, a 10-foot aura granting allies half cover, immunity to forced movement and prone, and one additional reaction each round that can only be used for Catch Them, Hold It!, Living Rampart or an opportunity attack. However, Kattal's speed becomes 0. He may end the effect at the beginning of any of his turns. He becomes exactly what the Nail has been teaching him to become since level 3: not the strongest creature on the battlefield, but the thing the battlefield cannot move.
